decision.explanation: The reference review initially prioritized the mean-centered Welch baseline, estimator/STFT spectral shape, carrier-band envelopes, harmonic spacing and impulsiveness because these views best separated the supplied recordings. Q01 is a valid, unclipped 10 s signal, but its dominant 89.6 Hz line and estimator concentration near 90 Hz are outside the dominant 44–46 Hz regime shared by all supplied references. The forced nearest reference is R06/C06 by baseline (3.332 dB), harmonic-spacing and persistence controls, but R06 conflicts in dominant-frequency hierarchy, 15 Hz envelope structure and filter-bank impulsiveness. Other small descriptive distances are inconsistent across views: R04/R06/R08 are closest cyclically, R05 in modulation map, R03 cepstrally, and R08/R04 in low impulsiveness. These are correlated views of the same signals and do not form independent votes. The strongest counterevidence to an outside-reference decision is the shared approximately 29.9 Hz harmonic family, but spacing candidates can arise from related tones and do not establish a condition. Numeric measurements and nearest-reference controls drive the ranking; no calibrated acceptance threshold is supplied, so nearest ranking is not acceptance. Orders and synchronous averages are unavailable for Q01 and every reference because no independent RPM trace was supplied [D03.orders, D03.synchronous, R01.orders, R01.synchronous, R02.orders, R02.synchronous, R03.orders, R03.synchronous, R04.orders, R04.synchronous, R05.orders, R05.synchronous, R06.orders, R06.synchronous, R07.orders, R07.synchronous, R08.orders, R08.synchronous]. Consequently, shaft/order attribution is unavailable, and neither fault component nor severity can be established. The best-supported conclusion is that Q01 is substantially different from all supplied condition references.
